issues.description: Wrong page is displaying. The current URL is /design/step-2 but we are evaluating step-3b. The screenshot shows step-1 (room selection), not step-3b (style blend confirmation with percentage bars). The page is either redirecting incorrectly or the router is broken.
issues.element: Entire page content - showing room selection instead of style blend confirmation
issues.root_cause: The URL shown is /design/step-2 but the page renders step-1 content. Either step-2 redirects to step-1, or the navigation flow is broken. The console logs show page:mount events for step-3 and step-3b, suggesting the app did navigate there but the screenshot was captured at step-2.

issues.description: Hydration error in step-3 page: Prop `style` did not match. Server: 'width:5%' Client: 'width:15%'. The percentage bar widths are being calculated differently on server vs client, causing full hydration failure and client re-render.
issues.root_cause: In apps/web/app/design/step-3/page.tsx, the width style for percentage bars is computed dynamically (likely from Math.random() or Date-based logic, or reading from localStorage/sessionStorage that isn't available on server). Server renders 5% but client computes 15%, causing mismatch.

issues.description: Multiple 'Text content does not match server-rendered HTML' errors causing entire root to switch to client rendering. This means step-3b likely shows broken/flash content.
issues.element: Text nodes in step-3 and step-3b pages
issues.root_cause: Style names or percentages are being read from client-only storage (localStorage/sessionStorage) or computed with non-deterministic logic during SSR, causing server/client HTML mismatch.

fixes.reason: Add a mounted guard so that dynamic/client-only values (percentages) are only rendered after hydration, preventing server/client mismatch.
Only apply the dynamic percentage width after client mount to prevent hydration mismatch between server (which can't read client state) and client.
Same hydration fix for step-3b page percentage bars to prevent server/client width mismatch.
